- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- codemyspec:design: Architecture design, UI design system, and technology strategy. Use before writing code to plan how to build it.
- codemyspec:develop: Full-lifecycle development — context orchestration, LiveView orchestration, and interactive refactoring. Spawns subagents for multi-step workflows.
- codemyspec:implement: Autonomous implementation loop — start or stop requirements-driven development. The agent walks the requirement graph automatically.
- codemyspec:init: Project setup, authentication, and sync. Use when starting a new project, logging in, or refreshing stale state.
- codemyspec:next: Find and start the next requirement task in one gesture. Use after each completed task as your single onboarding instruction.
- codemyspec:product: Product management — guided story interview, review, and Three Amigos sessions. Use when defining what to build, refining requirements, reviewing story quality, or running an Example Mapping session on a story.
- codemyspec:qa: QA testing and issue management — full app QA, per-story QA, integration planning, issue triage, and fixes.
- codemyspec:sync: Sync project components and regenerate architecture views. Use after git pulls, before design sessions, or when views feel stale.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).

First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

content.text: All 7 files exist as expected. Let me independently verify by fetching the Gherkin scenarios (which the subagent lacked access to) and checking that the delivered specs actually match, plus confirm compile/credo cleanliness myself.

Feature: Work each job from a room-by-room checklist with photo proof
  As a cleaner, I want each job to present a room-by-room checklist defining exactly what's in scope, with the ability to check off tasks and attach before/after photos, so that scope is never ambiguous and I'm protected from "missed spot" blame for tasks that weren't agreed to. (Research: scope ambiguity is the top cleaner frustration; photo checklists proven by STR tools — pain-points §2.1, §3.3)
  Rule: Each job presents a room-by-room checklist generated from that property's checklist template.
    Scenario: Checklist opens grouped by room
      Given my job's property has a checklist template with tasks for Kitchen, Bathroom, and Bedroom
      When I open the job's checklist
      Then I see the tasks grouped under Kitchen, Bathroom, and Bedroom
      And each task from the template appears under its room

  Rule: The checklist is the authoritative scope for the job: only tasks on the checklist are in scope, and completed checklists are retained as proof of what was agreed.
    Scenario: Out-of-scope task is not on the checklist
      Given my job's checklist does not include "clean inside oven"
      When I complete every task on the checklist and finish the job
      Then the completed checklist is retained showing no oven task
      And it serves as proof that cleaning inside the oven was out of scope

  Rule: A cleaner can check off individual checklist tasks, and the job shows progress as completed-of-total tasks.
    Scenario: Checking tasks advances progress
      Given my job's checklist has 10 tasks and none are checked
      When I check off 4 tasks
      Then the job shows progress as 4 of 10 tasks complete

  Rule: A cleaner can attach before and after photos to a task or room, each stored with a timestamp.
    Scenario: Before and after photos attach to a task
      Given I am working the Kitchen task on my job
      When I attach a before photo and an after photo to that task
      Then both photos are shown on the task
      And each photo is stored with the time it was captured

  Rule: A job can be marked complete only when every required task is checked and every required photo is attached.
    Scenario: Job completes when all required items are done
      Given every required task on my job is checked
      And every required photo is attached
      When I mark the job complete
      Then the job is accepted as complete

    Scenario: Completion blocked with a required task unchecked
      Given one required task on my job is still unchecked
      When I try to mark the job complete
      Then completion is blocked
      And I am told which required task or photo is still missing

  Rule: A photo upload that fails on poor connectivity is queued and retried, not silently dropped.
    Scenario: Photo taken offline uploads when signal returns
      Given I am in a home with no cell signal
      When I attach a photo to a task
      Then the photo is queued and marked as pending upload
      And when signal returns the photo uploads automatically without me re-taking it

defmodule CleanerCrmSpex.Story842.Criterion7172Spex do
  @moduledoc """
  Story 842 — Work each job from a room-by-room checklist with photo proof
  Criterion 7172 — Photo taken offline uploads when signal returns
  """

  use CleanerCrmSpex.Case

  import CleanerCrmSpex.SharedGivens

  alias CleanerCrmSpex.Fixtures

  spex "a checklist photo captured with no signal finishes uploading once connectivity returns" do
    scenario "photo taken offline uploads when signal returns" do
      given_ :logged_in_owner_with_account

      given_ "cleaner Ana is logged in on her assigned job with a checklist", context do
        client = Fixtures.client_fixture(context.scope)

        cleaner =
          Fixtures.cleaner_fixture(context.scope, context.account, %{email: "ana@example.com"})

        %{job: job, checklist: checklist} =
          Fixtures.job_with_checklist_fixture(context.scope, client, cleaner)

        conn = Fixtures.log_in_user(build_conn(), cleaner)

        {:ok,
         Map.merge(context, %{
           client: client,
           cleaner: cleaner,
           job: job,
           checklist: checklist,
           conn: conn
         })}
      end

      when_ "Ana captures the after photo of the first task while her phone has no signal",
            context do
        [task | _] = context.checklist.items

        {:ok, job_live, _html} = live(context.conn, ~p"/field/jobs/#{context.job.id}")

        upload =
          file_input(
            job_live,
            "[data-test='task-#{task.id}-after-photo-form']",
            :after_photo,
            [%{name: "after_kitchen.jpg", content: "after-photo-bytes", type: "image/jpeg"}]
          )

        render_upload(upload, "after_kitchen.jpg", 40)

        {:ok, Map.merge(context, %{job_live: job_live, task: task, upload: upload})}
      end

      then_ "the photo sits queued as a pending upload", context do
        assert has_element?(
                 context.job_live,
                 "[data-test='task-#{context.task.id}-photo-pending']"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end

      when_ "her signal returns", context do
        render_upload(context.upload, "after_kitchen.jpg", 100)

        {:ok, context}
      end

      then_ "the photo finishes uploading and is attached to the task", context do
        refute has_element?(
                 context.job_live,
                 "[data-test='task-#{context.task.id}-photo-pending']"
               )

        assert has_element?(
                 context.job_live,
                 "[data-test='task-#{context.task.id}-after-photo']"
               )

        {:ok, context}
      end
    end
  end
end
